item.title: APC chieftain rejects Baba-Ahmed’s 2027 election prediction
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Hon. Aminu Shehu Sharada, has faulted the National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Dr. Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, over his prediction that the ruling party could suffer significant losses in the 2027 general elections, particularly in northern Nigeria. Sharada, in a statement he personally signed on Thursday, insisted that President Bola Tinubu enjoys political support in the North and would secure votes from the region in the 2027 presidential election. He specifically rejected Baba-Ahmed’s projection that the APC would struggle to genuinely win even two or three states in northern Nigeria, describing the assessment as an underestimation of the political awareness, democratic maturity and independent judgment of voters in the region. Baba-Ahmed had, in an interview, said it would be a miracle if the APC genuinely won two or three states in the North, citing what he described as public dissatisfaction with the ruling party at different levels. “On the basis of the current disposition of the public towards APC at all levels, it will be a miracle if they genuinely win two or three states in the North,” he had said. He also predicted possible APC losses across the South-East, South-South, parts of the South-West and North-Central. However, Sharada argued that the political support enjoyed by Tinubu in northern Nigeria should not be dismissed on the basis of assumptions or projections by political commentators. Defending the Tinubu administration’s record, the APC chieftain highlighted its economic reforms, infrastructure projects and interventions in education, healthcare, agriculture, housing and transportation. He cited the removal of petrol subsidy, unification of the foreign exchange market and ongoing tax reforms as major policy decisions aimed at strengthening public finances and attracting investments. He acknowledged that the reforms had generated considerable debate because of their immediate effects on household expenses, transportation costs and the general cost of living, but maintained that the administration considered them necessary for long-term economic stability. On infrastructure, Sharada listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway and Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Road among major projects being pursued by the Federal Government. He also highlighted investments in railway modernisation, port improvements and electricity transmission. In education, he pointed to the establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying the initiative was designed to reduce financial barriers to higher education and improve access to tertiary education. He also cited the Renewed Hope housing programme, healthcare interventions under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and the Presidential Compressed Natural Gas Initiative as part of the administration’s development agenda. item.title: Tinubu should grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, Akande says
item.description: A former spokesman for ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande, has urged President Bola Tinubu to grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, saying the local media should have the opportunity to hold the President accountable. Akande made the call on Thursday while reacting to the controversy surrounding Tinubu’s interview with American political strategist and lobbyist, Diana London. He said he had no objection to the President granting an interview to a foreign journalist but questioned why Nigerian journalists had not been given similar opportunities to ask him questions on issues of national importance. “I wish the President were also having interviews with Nigerian journalists. That’s my own main issue with this development. “It’s not a bad thing that the President has chosen to have this interview; my worry is that he’s leaving out the Nigerian press. Why has he not made himself available for Nigerians to interrogate him?” he said. On allegations that London received $4.5 million in connection with the engagement, Akande said the strategist had denied being paid as a lobbyist by the Federal Government for the interview. He, however, called for greater transparency from the government to clarify the circumstances surrounding the engagement. “As to the controversy whether this woman (Diana) was paid, the woman has denied that she was doing this as a paid lobbyist of the Federal Government. The ADC people are saying that there should be more clarity, there should be more transparency, yes. “Let the Federal Government also give us more facts that this is not a paid-for interview. The most important thing is that Nigerians should be given the opportunity to interview Mr President,” Akande said. The former presidential spokesman also recalled his experience in the Presidential Villa during the administration of ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, when Osinbajo served as Vice-President. He said he considered it inappropriate for journalists invited to interview the President or Vice-President to demand payment for the opportunity. “My own experience in the Villa, I wasn’t aware of any payment for an interview and I expressed this. When we were in the Villa, I considered it an insult to have an opportunity to interview the President and the Vice-President and be asking for money. The President of a country is the numero uno,” he said. The controversy followed reports alleging that London received $4.5 million in connection with a lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government. London, who heads London Global Strategies, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government or anyone else in the country. She said she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to experience the country. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar also questioned whether the interview formed part of the reported $4.5 million lobbying arrangement. item.title: Court restrains Jimmy Odukoya from parading as Fountain of Life senior pastor
item.description: The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from parading himself as the Senior Pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin according to TheCable, granted the order on Wednesday following a suit instituted by the incorporated trustees of the church. The trustees had sought a pre-emptive order of injunction restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and interfering with its activities, governance and other affairs. They argued that Odukoya had ceased to hold the position following the appointment of a successor by the late founder and Senior Pastor of the church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. In the suit, the trustees sought an order restraining Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting, meddling with or obstructing the activities and governance of the church pending compliance with the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Directions No. 2 of 2019 on pre-action protocol. Granting the application, Justice Adewunmi-Oshin ruled: “Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to commence this action under the Pre-Action Protocol pursuant to Paragraph 4 of the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.” The order followed the trustees’ application for judicial intervention in the leadership and administration of the church. item.title: 2027: Atiku demands scrutiny of INEC’s AI system for processing election results
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to open its proposed artificial intelligence system for processing election results to independent audit ahead of the 2027 general elections. Atiku wants the commission to disclose how the technology works, who developed it and what safeguards are in place to prevent valid polling unit results from being flagged, delayed or excluded during electronic processing. In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said he had petitioned the INEC Chairman on behalf of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and allied democratic stakeholders, demanding algorithmic transparency, independent scrutiny and clear rules for human oversight. The petition follows INEC’s announced integration of artificial intelligence and intelligent document processing into the process linking its Data Verification and Authentication System, DIVAS, with the INEC Result Viewing portal, IReV. Warning against placing public confidence in an opaque technology, Atiku said: “INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward.” He demanded publication of the system’s technical and operational framework, including its training data sources, criteria for flagging discrepancies and the identities of its developers and third-party vendors. He also wants independent cybersecurity experts, political party technology representatives and civil society technologists to have access to the source code, training data and decision logs for a comprehensive audit before the nationwide mock accreditation scheduled for November 28, 2026. On the legal status of polling unit results, Atiku insisted that the physical Form EC8A, completed and signed at the polling unit, must remain the primary evidence of what transpired there, warning against allowing an algorithmic assessment to override it. “The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment. “A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents,” he said. Atiku also demanded a transparent procedure for reviewing flagged result sheets, including the officials responsible for such reviews, documentation of decisions, notification of political parties and mechanisms for promptly challenging errors. He proposed real-time monitoring access for political parties through a dedicated dashboard or observer interface to enable them to identify unusual patterns of flagging, delays or blocked uploads

item.title: Anambra home to political icons like Zik, Ekwueme, Soludo – Shettima
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – Vice-President Kashim Shettima has described Anambra State as a home of accomplished political leaders, citing Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe; former Vice-President, Dr. Alex Ekwueme; and the incumbent governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo. Shettima made the observation on Thursday at a joint mega rally organised by the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) under the banner of Progressives Working Together. The Vice-President, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the rally, said he was not surprised that Soludo had embraced what he described as the visionary politics of national unity associated with Azikiwe and Ekwueme. He commended the governor for what he described as his courage and political approach in the current political dispensation. Shettima also assured Nigerians, particularly residents of Anambra State, that Tinubu’s administration would reposition the country if given another term in 2027. In his remarks, Soludo said APGA and APC had unanimously endorsed Tinubu for a second term in office. As part of the alliance, the governor handed over the APGA flag to the APC, describing the move as a demonstration of the parties’ commitment to working together. Soludo further disclosed that elected APGA members in the state and National Assemblies would work with their APC counterparts in their respective legislative caucuses. He said the arrangement was aimed at promoting cooperation, national unity and the indivisibility of Nigeria. item.title: Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election, Soludo says
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, expressing confidence that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would win the contest. Soludo made the declaration on Thursday while speaking at a presidential campaign rally at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, where he argued that the APC had a stronger nationwide political presence than its opponents. “This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The president doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election,” he said. Explaining his position, the governor said the APC presidential ticket was facing opposition candidates whose political influence, according to him, was limited to certain parts of the country. “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shettima ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others. “If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic in your mind, this election is literally over,” Soludo said. He also attributed his confidence to the performance of the Tinubu administration, arguing that the President and Vice-President Kashim Shettima deserved another term based on their record in office. “President Tinubu, Shettima, they’re doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he said. The governor further argued that the APC had presented a stronger policy agenda than its opponents, claiming that no credible alternative had emerged ahead of the election. “And let me put it on record, in terms of the agenda that they are pursuing, no candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. “And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket presidency is on course,” he said. Soludo also defended the Federal Government’s handling of the economy and security, claiming that there was a consensus among people familiar with the economy, both locally and internationally, that the administration was moving in the right direction. He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which provides financial support to eligible students, as one of the initiatives through which the administration was addressing the needs of Nigerians. item.title: Kwara South: APC candidate Adewoye confident of victory
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general election, Prince Olalekan Adewoye, has expressed confidence in his ability to represent the people of the district effectively, saying his business experience and grassroots interventions have prepared him for public service. Adewoye said his conviction was anchored on more than three decades of experience in business, philanthropic activities and commitment to grassroots development. Speaking in an interview with journalists, the industrialist said he was passionate about translating his private-sector experience into public service, despite not having previously held an elective position or served as a political appointee. Addressing concerns about his lack of political experience and the challenge posed by established opposition politicians, Adewoye said he was confident of earning the support of voters. “I am convinced of my capacity and believe I have what it takes to represent the people effectively,” he said. He argued that voters should assess candidates based on their records, capacity and acceptability rather than previous political positions alone. According to him, his years in business have equipped him with the ability to manage people from different backgrounds, create value and deploy resources efficiently. He said these skills would be useful in legislative representation, particularly in ensuring that public resources and government programmes deliver tangible benefits to constituents. Adewoye disclosed that before joining the senatorial race, he had been involved in philanthropic activities through a foundation established to address some of the social and economic challenges facing residents of Kwara South. He identified healthcare, education and support for small businesses as critical areas requiring attention in the district. He said the foundation had provided equipment to individuals seeking to establish or expand businesses, supported healthcare interventions, including health insurance for elderly people, and assisted artisans and other vulnerable groups. According to him, the interventions were designed to promote self-reliance and economic independence rather than encourage beneficiaries to depend on periodic handouts. “We should not simply tell young people to look for jobs. We must help them acquire the skills, resources and support they need to create value,” he said. The APC candidate said his proposed representation would prioritise expanding economic opportunities for young people, traders, artisans and small business operators. He also disclosed plans to establish a trust fund to bring together individuals and organisations willing to support entrepreneurs and other deserving residents of Kwara South. item.title: Sanwo-Olu gives LASUED best graduate N5m, job
item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded the overall best graduating student of the Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), Blessed Mercy Olawunmi, with N5 million and automatic employment. The award was announced on Thursday, November 19, during the institution’s maiden convocation ceremony held at its Oto/Ijanikin campus. Olawunmi, of the Department of Home Economics, College of Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education, emerged top of the pioneering graduating class of 2,486 students, including 84 first-class graduates, with a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 4.98. Sanwo-Olu also announced a cash reward of N2.5 million each for the best graduating students from the university’s seven colleges. Apart from the governor’s award, Olawunmi received N250,000 and a commemorative plaque from the university, while Oto-Awori Local Government presented her with N1 million. The council chairman, Kareem Azeez Abiodun, also announced a reward of N500,000 each for the other best graduating students from the colleges. Speaking at the ceremony, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Bidemi Bilkis Lafiaji-Okuneye, thanked Sanwo-Olu for assenting to the law establishing the university in 2022. She also commended the Governing Council, staff, students and other stakeholders for their contributions towards making the institution a source of pride. However, she appealed to the governor to intervene in four areas requiring urgent attention: construction of a podcast and photojournalism studio, reconstruction of the perimeter fence, reclamation of swampy land at the main campus and completion of the 750-seat auditoriums at the Epe and Ijanikin campuses. The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that more than 60 per cent of the main campus land was swampy, leaving the institution with limited space for expansion. She said the university currently occupied only the dry portions of the land and was becoming increasingly cramped, adding that reclamation would provide room for future development. She noted that a female hostel being constructed by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) was already located on the site. “Your Excellency, sir, these four appeals are strategic investments rather than isolated requests. A studio will enrich what we teach. Secure fencing will protect people who teach — our land. Reclaimed land will create room for all that we still hope to build. An auditorium will provide a gathering space in which scholarship, professional development, and public engagement can flourish,” she said. Lafiaji-Okuneye also appreciated the Governing Council for its guidance and oversight, the Ministry of Tertiary Education for facilitating the university’s requests to the governor, and staff for sustaining the institution through its transition. item.description: Anambra State Governor, Charles Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to manipulate the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, insisting that his performance in office will earn him victory. Soludo said the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket of Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima was already in a strong position ahead of the election, arguing that no opposition candidate had presented a credible alternative to the ruling party. The governor spoke on Thursday at a 2027 presidential campaign rally in Anambra State attended by Shettima, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council Abdul’aziz Yari, former Anambra State governor Chris Ngige and Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, among other party chieftains. “To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shetima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others. “If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic. This election is literally over. President Tinubu and Shettima, they are doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he added. ﻿ Soludo also praised the Tinubu administration’s economic policies, security efforts and social intervention programmes, describing its agenda as superior to those presented by previous presidential candidates. “We know that there is still work to be done. And that work to be done means moving now from stability, having rescued the economy from total collapse, now moving into the next phase of shared prosperity. But let’s not kid ourselves. You don’t change a winning team. The Tinubu-Shetima ticket is the winning team,” the governor said. 2027 Presidential Election COMBO: Peter Obi, Atiku Abubakar, Bola Tinubu and Omoyele Sowore The 2027 presidential election, which is less than 60 days away, is expected to feature several prominent political figures, including Tinubu of the APC, Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC). item.title: 2027: APGA adopts Tinubu, says, you don’t change a winning team
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Grand Alliance APGA has presented its flag to President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate at the All Progressives Congress APC campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State. APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, announced the alliance at the rally held at Alex Ekwueme Square on Thursday. “The chairman of PDP is not here, but he is well in his spirit. The chairman of Accord is here. We are four in one. Four political parties supporting one candidate. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Yilwatda then invited Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, to present the APGA flag, with Vice President Kashim Shettima receiving it on Tinubu’s behalf. Soludo said the handover made the rally unlike any other. He said it was the first time APGA was presenting its flag to the Tinubu/Shettima ticket as its presidential candidate. He also reminded the crowd that Anambra was where the ticket did worst in 2023. According to him, it recorded 5,111 votes, or 0.8 per cent. “Ndi Anambra, are we going to do far better than 2023? We will not be there again,” he said. The governor said Ndigbo would lose from another round of political isolation. “Let us make this campaign a conversation, not an argument among ourselves. In a democracy, what leverage do we have other than our votes and having alliance with the rest of the country?There is work to be done, but you don’t change a winning team”, he said. Soludo said power would move to the North in 2031 and that the South should first complete its eight years. He also said the contest was already decided. “This election, to the best of my knowledge, is already won and lost. No candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative,” he said. Yilwatda said the President had shown confidence in the Southeast by giving its sons key roles. He named the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, who he said is constructimg good roads. He said even the opposition used those roads. “Even Peter Obi is using our roads. Atiku is using our roads. Those roads are constructed by your son, Umahi,” he said. Yilwatda described Tinubu as the most experienced and formidable of the candidates, pointing to his record as Lagos State governor and at the centre. He said the President had stabilised the economy and fixed roads, power and education. item.title: Man accused of AI-assisted exam cheating found dead in Seoul
item.description: A South Korean man suspected of using artificial intelligence (AI) to obtain a perfect score in the country’s law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul. Lee Jin-woo was discovered at a motel in Cheonho-dong, Gangdong District, eastern Seoul, at about 1:12 p.m. on Thursday, emergency authorities said. According to Yonhap News TV, a note was also found at the scene, reportedly indicating that Lee was physically and mentally exhausted. However, the note reportedly contained no admission of cheating or explanation of the allegations against him. Authorities said they would examine the scene to establish the circumstances surrounding his death. Lee had attracted public attention over allegations that he used AI to cheat in the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET), the examination required for admission into law schools in South Korea. In an attempt to dispel the suspicions, he had announced plans to answer questions from the Korean language section of the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test in real time on Thursday morning. However, he failed to appear at the designated venue by 8:40 a.m., when the examination began. Police launched a search after receiving a report at about 8:42 a.m. expressing concern over his whereabouts. According to the police, Lee left his home on Wednesday and travelled to a lodging facility in Gwangjin District, eastern Seoul, before leaving on Thursday morning. He reportedly took a taxi towards Songpa District, southern Seoul, between 8 a.m. and 9 a.m., before heading to Gangdong District, where his body was later discovered. Lee had previously gained attention after revealing that he had scored between the sixth and eighth tiers in previous college entrance examinations, which use a nine-tier grading system, with higher numbers representing lower scores. He said he later developed a better understanding of studying and reading comprehension, eventually gaining admission into Korea University’s Department of Political Science and International Relations in 2024 and Seoul National University’s School of Dentistry in 2026. He also reportedly achieved a perfect score in the LEET while attending Seoul National University. However, his academic achievements came under scrutiny following allegations of AI-assisted cheating in a national tax accountant certification examination. Questions were subsequently raised over whether he had also used AI to cheat in the LEET and the college entrance examinations for the 2024 and 2026 academic years. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said on Wednesday that it had assigned a criminal complaint against Lee, bordering on allegations of obstruction of business, obstruction of official duties and fraud, to its Provincial Special Detective Corps. Following his death, police are expected to close the case without prosecution, as criminal proceedings cannot continue against a deceased suspect. item.title: Fountain of Life Church postpones 2026 Thanksgiving service
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving service, earlier scheduled for Sunday, November 22, amid an ongoing leadership crisis involving Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and members of its Board of Trustees. The Lagos-based church announced the postponement in a notice shared on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19. The notice read, “Please be informed that our Thanksgiving 2026 Service, previously scheduled for Sunday, November 22, has been postponed. A new date will be communicated in due course.” The church did not give any reason for the decision or indicate when the service would be rescheduled. The development comes amid a leadership dispute following an announcement by some members of the Board of Trustees withdrawing recognition of Odukoya as the church’s senior pastor with immediate effect. The trustees reportedly based their decision on a review of the church’s constitution and a December 2021 video recording in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, outlined succession arrangements that identified another individual as his preferred successor, while assigning Jimmy Odukoya administrative and youth church responsibilities. They also cited governance concerns and issues surrounding Odukoya’s recent remarriage. However, Odukoya and representatives of the church rejected the announcement, describing it as constitutionally invalid and not a decision properly taken by the Board of Trustees. They maintained that he remains the duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the board, following his unanimous approval for the positions in September 2023 after his father’s death. The trustees subsequently reaffirmed their position and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to provide interim spiritual and administrative leadership pending further consultations. The crisis has also extended to the control of the church’s official social media accounts, with both sides reportedly disputing authority over the platforms. Odukoya was notably absent from the church’s midweek service on Thursday as the leadership dispute continued. The Thanksgiving service had attracted attention amid the unfolding crisis, with the postponement adding another development to the dispute over the church’s leadership and administration. item.title: Road crashes fall 13.8%, deaths drop to 941 in Q3 2026 — FRSC
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has reported a 13.8 per cent reduction in road traffic crashes across Nigeria in the third quarter of 2026, with fatalities dropping from 1,077 in the corresponding period of 2025 to 941. The Corps also recorded a decline in the number of people injured, from 6,856 to 5,864, representing a 14.5 per cent reduction. The figures were disclosed in a statement on Thursday by the Corps Public Education Officer, Osondu Ohaeri, following the end-of-year strategy session with commanding officers at the FRSC headquarters in Abuja. According to the statement, 2,098 road traffic crashes were recorded between July and September 2026, compared with 2,434 in the corresponding period of 2025. The reduction of 336 crashes exceeded the Corps’ 10 per cent reduction target. Similarly, the number of people injured dropped by 992, while fatalities declined by 136, representing a 12.6 per cent reduction. The statement said, “A comparative assessment of the two periods shows that road traffic crashes declined from 2,434 in Q3 2025 to 2,098 in Q3 2026, representing 336 fewer crashes. “Road traffic injuries also dropped significantly from 6,856 to 5,864, a reduction of 992, while recorded fatalities decreased from 1,077 to 941, representing 136 fewer deaths.” The Corps attributed the improvement to enhanced patrol operations, crash prevention measures, public education and enforcement of traffic laws. Ahead of the 2026 festive season, the Corps Marshal, Shehu Mohammed, directed commanding officers nationwide to intensify patrol operations along high-risk routes, improve traffic management and strengthen collaboration with other security and emergency response agencies. He also ordered the strategic deployment of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, while directing commands to sustain public awareness campaigns on safe driving. “As the nation approaches the 2026 festive season, the Corps Marshal has directed Commanding Officers across the country to translate the gains recorded into more effective highway operations, with particular attention to strategic patrol deployment along high-risk corridors, improved traffic management, stronger collaboration with sister agencies, strategic positioning of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, and sustained public enlightenment,” the statement added. Mohammed also urged commanding officers to strengthen supervision, prioritise personnel welfare and enforce discipline, warning that the Corps would maintain zero tolerance for extortion, negligence and abuse of authority. In his remarks, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, said the figures reflected progress made under the reforms introduced by the Corps Marshal, particularly the increased emphasis on technology and operational intelligence. item.title: ‎2027: APGA endorses Tinubu
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) on Thursday adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate and handed him the party’s flag. ‎ ‎Governor Charles Soludo and the party’s national chairman handed the flag to President Tinubu at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign event in Awka, Anambra State. ‎ ‎Prof. Soludo said, “We resolved, in the spirit of one Nigeria, progressivism, cooperative federalism, unity and the progress of our indivisible, united Nigeria, to hand our flag to Prese ent Tinubu.” ‎ ‎He said all APGA members would canvass votes for President Tinubu. ‎He advocated political engagement and bridge-building rather than what he described as isolationism, saying this approach would ensure regional prosperity. ‎ ‎Soludo said Ndigbo should adopt a political strategy that rejects political isolation and ethnic intolerance, noting that such attitudes limit political leverage and risk wasting productive years through internal conflict. ‎ ‎He encouraged building bridges towards a united nation where all citizens could thrive, regardless of their location or ethnicity. He also asserted that the 2027 election was effectively decided in favour of the Tinubu/Shettima ticket. ‎ ‎He claimed that no other presidential candidate had presented a credible alternative or a superior manifesto. He added that there was significant consensus on the administration’s approach to security and economic stability, which he credited with rescuing the economy from collapse. ‎ ‎The governor described wasting political opportunities as a high-stakes mistake with significant long-term consequences. He stressed that solidarity with the Tinubu government was a means of securing future political influence in 2027. ‎ ‎For his part, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, advocated a shift from sentimental politics to strategic cooperation to drive development in Anambra State and the wider South-East. ‎ ‎He argued that the success of Igbo people in business and commerce stems from strategic thinking rather than sentiment. ‎ ‎He suggested that political progress requires moving away from protest-based approaches and focusing instead on strategic alliances. item.title: Africa Records 71.4bn Transactions, $1.8trn Instant Payments In 2025 — Report
item.description: Africa’s instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly three times the volume recorded in 2021, according to a new report by the AfricaNenda Foundation, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group. The fifth edition of the State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report, published on Thursday, highlighted the rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructure across the continent but warns that access alone has not translated into widespread everyday usage. According to the report, 89 per cent of African adults live in countries with access to an instant payment system. However, a survey of 1,403 digital payment users across 15 markets found that 55 per cent still use cash for about half of their transactions. It also found that more than half of respondents had experienced payment problems, including delays and transfers to the wrong recipients, while one in three affected users never reported such incidents, largely because they did not know how to do so. “Five years ago, our first report mapped 29 instant payment systems; today there are 39, and one in two African adults live in a country served by an inclusive instant payment system IIPS,” said Sabine F. Mensah, who is Deputy CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation and lead author of the report. “The question has changed. It is no longer whether Africans can pay instantly, but whether they trust the system enough to stop reaching for cash. Our research shows that trust is won in seconds, through a payment that goes through instantly, with preventive safeguards such as recipient name validation, and a payment confirmation message received in real time. It is kept by getting timely resolution and people’s money back when something goes wrong.” (L-R): Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Sabine Mensah; CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Robert Ochola; and Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Akinwale Goodluck, at the report launch on Thursday, November 19, 2026. 39 Instant Payment Systems The report identified 39 live instant payment systems across Africa, comprising 35 domestic systems in 29 countries and four regional systems. Overall, 43 African countries now have access to instant payment capabilities through domestic or regional platforms. Four domestic systems were introduced in the past year in Liberia, Burundi, Guinea and Mauritania, while a new regional system now serves the eight countries of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). Another 17 countries have instant payment system projects underway. Transaction volumes, according to the report, have grown by an average of 28 per cent annually since 2021, while the average transaction value has declined from $45 to $26, indicating increased use for smaller, everyday purchases. item.title: [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally
item.description: There was a mild drama at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State on Thursday when a former governor of the state, Chris Ngige, urged residents to vote for the APC in the 2027 presidential, National Assembly, and House of Assembly elections. The former Minister of Labour and Employment, who spoke in Igbo, said Anambra residents had one target. “We will vote for the APC from top to bottom,” Ngige said, prompting reactions from participants at the rally, including Governor Charles Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), who stood beside him on stage and told his predecessor that the rally is a joint one. The former governor, who said he was not surprised by the reactions, later told members of APGA to vote for candidates of their choice. “Okay, members of APGA — freedom of choice — when you get to the polling booth, vote for the better place,” he said. Ngige added that while people were free to choose between APGA and the APC, Anambra desires to be connected to the Federal Government at the centre and get it through the ruling party. Earlier, the former minister said he remains a member of the APC, claiming that he brought the party to the South-East. “I am still a member of the APC, bona fide member, because I brought APC to the South East — 2013/2014,” he said. “The only thing is that I told people I am on sabbatical, but even if I am on sabbatical, my governor cannot be doing something, and the Vice President is coming physically, and the governor has called me to say we are here, and I would say I won’t come. No.” Ngige said people should not be forced but persuaded to vote during the 2027 general election. He also said those stopping people from campaigning are not doing so in the name of the APC. “We don’t want that — destruction of vehicles, stoning of people. No! We don’t want that. We must emulate other people practising democracy,” the former Anambra governor said. “Democracy gives you the right of choice; even inside the same family, you must exercise that.” Watch Ngige’s remarks in the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally appeared first on Channels Television .
